assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another at a target site without double-strand cleavage, using a deaminase tethered to a Cas protein. It rests on a clear chemical principle (hydrolytic or enzymatic deamination within a defined editing window), gives a quantitative and general capability, and has opened a large space of therapeutic and research applications, including clinical trials. It fits well with my wish for a principle plus a genuinely new capability.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive contributions; Komor developed the cytosine base editors and Gaudelli the adenine base editors (which needed directed evolution of a TadA deaminase). Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were close in time and complicate a strict three-person claim. Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is the cleanest configuration but the supplied credit does not settle the Japanese contribution.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups and by first clinical use; only about a decade old, so timing is somewhat early but not premature. Sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, which the committee may see as a relevant precedent.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to treat base and prime editing together (B048) rather than base editing alone
Priority claim of Kondo and Nishida for Target-AID relative to Komor and Gaudelli
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, via sequencing-by-synthesis on a surface with reversible terminator chemistry (Solexa/Illumina) and the pyrosequencing-in-picolitre-wells approach of 454, cut the cost of reading a genome by many orders of magnitude. The underlying chemistry (nucleotide design, single-molecule and cluster fluorescence detection) is clear and quantitative, and the impact on biology and medicine is vast.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry; Rothberg led the 454 emulsion-PCR and picolitre-reactor platform. Mayer and Ju contributed related ideas (Ju on terminators, Mayer on parallel clonal arrays), so credit is plural and a three-person split needs a deliberate choice about which platforms to honour.
assessment.maturity: Technology has been mature and validated for fifteen or more years; recognition is overdue rather than early. Sanger sequencing was already honoured in 1980, and the committee must be able to state what chemistry is new.
uncertainties: Allocation among competing platforms and between chemists, engineers and company founders
Whether the committee regards it as chemistry rather than biotechnology or physiology or medicine

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopores read single DNA or RNA molecules as they are threaded through a pore and modulate an ionic current. This is the sort of physics-meets-chemistry principle I appreciate: single-molecule transport measured electrically, with direct readout of base identity, long reads and modification detection, and a commercial instrument. It opens the possibility of portable sequencing and protein analysis.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed the concept and early experiments; Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin in 1996; Bayley engineered pores, and Akeson showed enzymatic control of the strand, which made reading practical. Choosing three is difficult, and I am unsure of the current status of some of these scientists (a laureate must be living).
assessment.maturity: Concept dates from the 1990s, and long-read nanopore sequencing has been used widely for over a decade, with a robust independent literature. Timing is appropriate, though accuracy remains improving.
uncertainties: Several essential contributors, so a three-person allocation is contested
Whether any key contributor is deceased, which I cannot verify from the supplied text
Overlap with the sequencing field covered by B043

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles encapsulate nucleic acids through a pH-dependent charge switch, enabling intracellular delivery and endosomal escape. This is the enabling chemistry behind siRNA therapy and the mRNA vaccines; the physical-chemistry principle (pKa tuning, lipid phase behaviour) is clear and the impact was demonstrated at global scale.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues in Vancouver (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable lipid concept; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and screening. The 2023 medicine prize recognised the mRNA modification, leaving delivery as a natural complement, but the credit is spread over many people and companies.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale since 2018 (Onpattro) and 2020 (COVID vaccines); strongly confirmed. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Complex allocation between Vancouver founders and the MIT group
Possible view that the 2023 medicine prize already covered this topic

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from about 4 percent to over 25 percent within about a decade, which is exceptional. The underlying physics (defect tolerance, long carrier diffusion lengths, tunable band gap by composition) is a clear principle and the materials chemistry is simple solution processing. Generative potential extends to LEDs and detectors.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009; Park developed the solid-state 2012 device and Snaith the thin-film mesoscopic and planar architectures. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed significantly, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency record is widely replicated, but long-term stability and commercialisation are unresolved, which argues that recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Operational stability and toxicity of lead
Many strong contributors beyond three
Whether the committee waits for commercial deployment

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle for membraneless compartments connects polymer physics and thermodynamics with cell biology. It changed how cellular organisation is understood and is conceptually simple and general, with applications in disease and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids (2009); Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase transitions in 2012. Pappu and Mittag supplied physical-chemical theory and sequence grammar. A fair three-person split is feasible but debatable.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing but contested: how far in vivo condensates are functional phase-separated liquids versus other assemblies is still debated, so the interpretation is not stable yet.
uncertainties: Debate on whether in vivo condensates are true phase separation
Possible fit with medicine or physics rather than chemistry
Quantitative evidence is variable across systems

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs allows site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells, making proteins programmable at the atomic level. It is original, clear, and has generated a wide range of tools and applications in biophysics and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems (2001); Chin extended this to quadruplet codons, orthogonal ribosomes and whole-organism recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed. Three people are reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and used by many groups for over twenty years; timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Competing claims for early priority
Whether the committee sees it as an extension of the 2018 directed evolution prize or the 2024 protein prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses ultrashort X-ray free-electron-laser pulses to outrun radiation damage ('diffraction before destruction'), allowing room-temperature structures of microcrystals and time-resolved chemistry on femtosecond scales. This has the quality of approaching a physical limit and offers a capability not possible before.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the concept and early demonstrations, Fromme and Schlichting contributed the first protein crystal experiments and sample delivery; Hajdu proposed the concept. Neutze and others also contributed. Hajdu's status (deceased 2021 per my recollection, uncertain) matters.
assessment.maturity: Methods validated at multiple facilities, but the number of transformative chemistry results is still modest and access is limited, which argues for later recognition.
uncertainties: Whether Hajdu is still living
Limited facilities and the modest number of landmark scientific outcomes so far
Fit with physics or structural biology
